_why: THE CONTRACT BETWEEN THE SHELL AND A BATCH. Every token and every data const the report needs is listed here ONCE, with where it comes from and whether it is required. fill_verify.mjs reads this file and refuses to let a report be published that is missing, empty or stale. It exists because two failures kept recurring and neither was visible on the page: batch-specific prose baked into the shell got republished verbatim for a different batch (the flatcost 'next lever' shipped under canon-n7, every sentence wrong), and data sections the fill scripts did not populate rendered as empty tables rather than saying so.
_rule: The shell holds STRUCTURE. Prose that names a year, a country, a run or a number is a TOKEN, filled from a file. Numbers are CONSTS, derived by a fill_*.mjs. Nobody hand-edits the assembled REPORT.html - it is an artifact, and an edit there is lost on the next fill.

tokens.name: __SESSION__
tokens.means: session folder name; also the staleness key

tokens.name: __ARM__
tokens.means: arm kind + the frozen config and its sha

tokens.name: __N__
tokens.means: runs COUNTED, after L17 excludes incomplete ones

tokens.name: __GAME__
tokens.means: game build every run actually ran on

tokens.name: __DELTA__
tokens.means: what changed vs the previous batch's arm

tokens.name: __BASE__
tokens.means: comparison baseline + whether it is same-night

tokens.name: __LEDE__
tokens.means: what this batch is for, and how to read the table

tokens.name: __GOALS__
tokens.means: G-rows; POSITIONAL: metric A B -> value A B -> target A B

tokens.name: __INCIDENTS__
tokens.means: confounds THIS batch carries; must name its own runs

tokens.name: __NEXT__
tokens.means: the lever this batch's numbers point at

tokens.name: __FOOTER__
tokens.means: provenance: what was read, how many, on what build

tokens.name: __ARMLABEL__
tokens.means: legend label of THIS arm's GDP line (was the literal 'flat 0.65×' in the shell: every report since flatcost-n1 labelled its own arm with the flatcost arm's name)

tokens.name: __NBLABEL__
tokens.means: legend label of the reference (NB) series (was the literal '×1.5^era')

tokens.name: __VANLABEL__
tokens.means: how the GDP chart names the vanilla baseline, e.g. 'n=16 median' (was 'n=4 mean')

tokens.name: __SPREAD__
tokens.means: the sentence after 'A median hides the spread —': this batch's per-run GDP ratio range at 1935 and how to read it (was a literal 0.59–1.02× from an earlier batch)

consts.name: GDP_FLAT
consts.means: yearly world GDP, this arm, median of runs

consts.name: EMP
consts.means: tier employment by era, EXACT (staffed levels x per-tier employment)

consts.name: TRAJ
consts.means: GDP / levels / construction, each divided by vanilla

consts.name: LADDER
consts.means: climb and death: most-built era, e0 share, frontier/stale payback, staffing

consts.name: WATCH
consts.means: watchlist summary row per anchor year

consts.name: PERF
consts.means: row P. byYear is YEARS PER MINUTE; model keys are c0/cPop/cLv

consts.name: VA
consts.means: tiered-sector value added + its coverage counts

consts.name: D2
consts.means: per-country dataset; must carry techsT + jeT (fill_research.mjs supplies them)

consts.name: TIERC
consts.means: build choice: below-best share (F75 basis: raw/unit-weighted/ex-ports) + the below-best-AND-less-efficient-than-frontier share (tier_profit §c) — user-required 2026-08-24

consts.name: INDECOMP
consts.means: industry composition of VALUE ADDED: {years, mod, van}, each year {ind, broad, tags} - absolute GBP/wk so the renderer can follow scope + selection; user-required 2026-08-24, permanent, BOTH pages

tables.means: build choice - construction below the frontier

staleness._why: A report that still names a PREVIOUS batch is the failure that prompted this file. These strings must NOT appear in a freshly filled report; add each retired session id and arm label as it is superseded.
